A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conditional conformal test martingale research. The main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A-H are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of error control and detection power, ImageNet-C evaluations, and appendix experiments on clipping and pairwise betting.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports a revised delayed-change experiment in Section 4.1 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The fixed-reference construction, confidence-band correction, smoothed betting function, ONS updates, and clipping procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1-2 retain the same steps; mixture martingales are discussed only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Gaussian immediate, delayed, and gradual shifts, Gaussian AR(1) sequences, and ImageNet-C corruptions. The revised change-point timing is a setting change within the existing delayed-shift task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: standard CTM in the principal comparisons, invalid CTM in Figure 2, and pairwise betting in the AR(1) experiment. Newly discussed mixture martingales are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Figure 3 replace the delayed-change settings {200, 400, 600} with {200, 600, 4000}. The reference size, distributions, testing parameters, and other experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The delay-sensitivity analysis now examines a substantially longer period before the shift, testing how accumulated null observations affect detection. The clipping ablation in Appendix F and other supplementary analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 trials for Figure 3 and retain the other simulation repetition counts. ImageNet-C still uses 10 seeds and the same standard-error reporting. No new uncertainty-estimation practice or significance test appears.

E6.justification: Figure 3 replaces the 400-step-delay results with 4000-step-delay results. In the new condition, standard CTM initially leads before conditional CTM overtakes it. The immediate-shift and gradual-shift panels, ImageNet-C results, and appendix figures are unchanged; this is not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, regret analysis, and proofs in Appendices D-E are unchanged. The added explanation of conditional validity and remark comparing stopping-time bounds clarify existing mathematics without adding a formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and principal concluding claims retain the same scope: avoiding reference contamination, conditional anytime validity, power and stopping-time guarantees, and improved empirical detection. The new qualifications concern interpretation and limitations.

C2.justification: v2 explains the initial standard-CTM advantage after a long null period and its subsequent loss through contamination. Section 5 newly states that mean-based betting can miss shifts preserving the p-value mean, and discusses ONS versus mixture martingales and the latter's unresolved power guarantees.

D1.justification: A new footnote in Section 1 provides a repository link for a software package implementing the method. This adds code-access information; the implementation details in Appendix H are unchanged, and repository contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Clerico's two works, Gauthier et al., Kaufmann and Koolen, and Timans et al. These provide limited additional positioning around betting optimality, comparable stopping-time bounds, mixture martingales, and risk monitoring, without reorganizing the research framing.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanatory passages, expands the discussion, and introduces acknowledgments, funding disclosure, and an impact statement. The publication footer changes to conference proceedings information. The main section order and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 3's middle panel has revised delay labels, curves, and a broader horizontal axis. Figure 4 moves from the left to the right column on page 8, with accompanying text reflow. Other figure contents and appendix layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: Replacing the intermediate delay with a 4000-step stress test reveals an initial baseline advantage and supports a more nuanced empirical interpretation. The explicit limitation concerning mean-preserving shifts, additional theoretical context, and software-access link improve transparency and usefulness. These are limited gains; the method, formal guarantees, and most empirical evidence remain unchanged.
